paragraphs: A marketplace platform becomes more valuable to each seller as more buyers join, and more valuable to each buyer as more sellers join. This mutual reinforcement explains why such platforms often grow slowly at first and then very quickly, and why a late entrant, even one with a technically superior product, can find it nearly impossible to attract either group: sellers will not come without buyers, and buyers will not come without sellers. Entrants sometimes break the deadlock by subsidizing one side, usually buyers, in the expectation that the other side will follow. The strategy is costly, and it works only if the subsidized group, once the subsidy ends, finds enough reason to stay.
